note: Happy Thanksgiving: the 100th Macy's parade moves to Saturday, Susan's email hits the group chat, and the September polar bear meme finally sees its month arrive.

segments.title: Balloons Down: The 100th Macy's Parade Moves to Saturday
segments.why_trending: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been moved from Thursday to Saturday, Nov 28, because of a projected severe storm. ABC News and CNN reported it is the first postponement in the parade's 100-year history.
talking_points: ABC News and CNN reported this is the first time the parade has been postponed in its 100 years, and it happened in the 100th year.
Per TheWrap (Nov 25), Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a State of Emergency for NYC, Long Island and Westchester, and balloons that were already inflated had to be deflated.
Spectators interviewed by ABC 7 were surprised by the move, and some tourists said they would change their travel plans.
For viewers at home: NBC re-airs the 2025 parade Thursday at 8:30 a.m. and airs the 2026 parade in the same slot on Saturday, with Raye opening the broadcast.
host_questions: Does Thanksgiving morning feel like Thanksgiving without a live parade on TV?
If you had a ticket to New York for the parade, would you change your trip or stay and make a weekend of it?
Is moving the parade two days later the right call, or should a 100-year tradition try to stick to Thursday whenever it can?
segments.angle: Keep it neutral: a 100-year first, made for safety reasons, and the practical details of what changes for viewers and visitors.

segments.title: Dear Family, Per Susan: The Thanksgiving Email Everyone Recognizes
segments.why_trending: A fictional Thanksgiving planning email from "Susan," a controlling mother-in-law, went viral after screenshots spread without context (NBC, Nov 24). It comes from creator Kristen Knutson's series "The Kayla Files."
talking_points: Susan is a character from Kristen Knutson's series "The Kayla Files," but screenshots of the email spread without that context.
She was written as the villain, yet many viewers found Susan relatable instead.
Per NBC, the videos have drawn 6M+ views and thousands of comments.
It landed right in Thanksgiving week, when plenty of real family planning emails are flying around.
host_questions: Is Susan the villain, or is she just the only person actually organizing Thanksgiving?
Who is the Susan in your family, and would they admit it?
What's one rule you'd put in your own Thanksgiving planning email?
segments.angle: Debate framing: villain or hero? The joke works because half the audience sees a control freak and the other half sees the one person holding the holiday together.

clips.title: A fictional Thanksgiving email went viral for its painfully relatable family dynamics.
clips.creator: @NBCPhiladelphia

segments.title: 3.5 Billion Views: GTA 6 Takes Over YouTube
segments.why_trending: Per Tech4Gamers (Nov 24), YouTube said GTA 6-related videos drew 3.5B+ views on launch day. On Nov 24, a track from GTAVI: The Album hit #1 on YouTube's US trending chart.
talking_points: YouTube said GTA 6 videos drew 3.5B+ views on launch day; pre-launch GTA 6 videos had already passed 40B, and the franchise overall has passed 900B (per Tech4Gamers).
The game's music is charting too: a track from GTAVI: The Album hit #1 on YouTube US trending on Nov 24, and the Travis Scott version also charted.
The trending list also included GTA 6 videos like "GTA 6 just exposed every game critic.." and SML's "Brooklyn Guy Plays GTA 6."
It's not just gameplay: music, commentary and comedy sketches are all riding the launch.
host_questions: Would you rather play GTA 6 or watch other people play it?
Can a video game soundtrack really compete with regular chart music now?
Is there anything else in entertainment right now that could pull 3.5 billion views in a day?
segments.angle: GTA 6 isn't just a game launch, it's a whole YouTube ecosystem: a number-one song, comedy sketches and critic debates all in the same week.

segments.title: Doom Is Coming: The Avengers: Doomsday Final Trailer
segments.why_trending: Marvel's final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday held #2 on YouTube's US trending chart in every check on Nov 24 (trendoday). The film opens in theaters Dec 18.
talking_points: The trailer stayed at #2 on YouTube US trending in every check on Nov 24, per trendoday.
It's surrounded on the chart by breakdown and reaction videos covering Easter eggs, Doctor Doom and the X-Men.
New Rockstars posted a reaction and Q&A, one of the reaction videos riding the trailer.
The film opens in theaters Dec 18, about three weeks out.
host_questions: Do you watch the trailer breakdowns, or do they spoil too much?
What would it take for this movie to feel like a true event again?
Are you seeing it opening weekend, or waiting for streaming?
segments.angle: The trailer is only half the story: the breakdown and reaction videos around it are their own trending genre.

segments.title: My Moon My Maaaan: The Couples Swipe Trend
segments.why_trending: Couples are posting two-photo slideshows with "my moon my maaaan" stretched across both images for a swipe reveal, set to FINNEAS's live cover of Feist's 2007 song (KYM, Nov 23). The cover hit No. 1 on TikTok's worldwide trending audio chart, per BroadwayWorld (Nov 20).
talking_points: The format: two photos, one caption stretched across both, so the swipe completes the line.
The FINNEAS version took off from Nov 7 and spread to Instagram by mid-November; @zizigoeazy's post got 1.9M+ likes in five days and @marnie_s04's got about 1.6M.
BroadwayWorld reports the cover hit No. 1 on TikTok's worldwide trending audio chart and is now on all streaming platforms.
The original is getting a boost too: Feist's version rose 61% in US on-demand streams, to 4.3M+ in a week, per Billboard.
host_questions: Is a couples trend cute or cringe, and does it depend on the couple?
Which old song deserves a cover that sends it back up the charts?
Would you post one, and who would you be the moon and who the man?
segments.angle: A 2007 song gets a second life through a live cover and a swipe trick, and the original artist benefits too.

segments.title: Remember November 2026? The Polar Bear Was Right on Time
segments.why_trending: A September meme about an AI polar bear singing "Remember November 2026 is coming" has reached its "prophecy" month. Now that it's actually November 2026, Know Your Meme is running a November meme-of-the-month poll.
talking_points: It started with a 2023 AI polar bear image joked to be "from the future," November 2026; KYM puts that origin TikTok at about 3.1M plays.
In late August 2026, @bigbakdiskk28 revived it with an AI polar bear singing "Remember November 2026 is coming" to Oliver Tree's "Life Goes On," and it spread on TikTok and Reels in September (KYM).
One spin-off showed a polar bear beside a chips bag expiring November 2026, which got 92K+ likes in three days per KYM.
The month is here, and KYM's November meme-of-the-month poll is running.
host_questions: So it's November 2026. Did anything the polar bear warned us about actually happen?
Why do 'from the future' memes hit so hard?
What date-based meme should the internet start now for a few years out?
segments.angle: A good closer: the internet spent September waiting for a month that has finally arrived, and the payoff may just be Thanksgiving.
